record.excerpt: So basically I use 5EMA and also use a 50EMA ( for trend basically ) then I set my RSI to 5 also… … So once your 5ema crosses your 50ema and RSI cross the 50 line, boom there is your signal, … I do like to wait for the candle of that day to close though, … since this week I started using it on the daily and 4 hour charts … So far I have opened 4 trades at 8pm last night (20/08/2013) on USD/CAD, EUR/USD, GBP/USD, and also EUR/JPY.
record.performance_claim: usd/cad has moved just over 200 pips in my favour
record.notes: Forex EMA5/50 + RSI(5) cross 50 rule; no page date header, in-text date 20/08/2013 implies post ~2013-08-21.

spec.claim_summary: Enter when the 5-period EMA crosses the 50-period EMA and the 5-period RSI crosses the 50 line.
assumptions: Direction not stated as long-only; 'crosses' compiled as crosses_above for long entry.

NOT EXPRESSIBLE: claim implies both long and short signals from crosses in either direction but schema direction allows only long or short, so the short side (5EMA crosses below 50EMA with RSI crossing below 50) is omitted.
NOT EXPRESSIBLE: claim states use on both the daily and 4 hour charts but schema timeframe allows only one value, so only 1d is tested and the 4h variant is omitted.
No exit stated; exit by opposite EMA cross (5EMA crosses below 50EMA) used as most common reading for MA-cross setup.
Waiting for candle close is default bar-close evaluation.

evidence.quote: on USD/CAD, EUR/USD, GBP/USD, and also EUR/JPY
on the daily and 4 hour charts

issues.problem: Claim says '5ema crosses your 50ema and RSI cross the 50 line' with no long-only limit, implying signals in both directions. Spec restricts to direction=long with crosses_above only and omits the short side (5EMA crosses below 50EMA with RSI crossing below 50).
Claim explicitly says strategy used 'on the daily and 4 hour charts'. Spec tests only timeframe 1d and omits the 4h variant.
Claimant states no exit rule. Spec invents exit by opposite EMA cross (5EMA crosses_below 50EMA), which adds a holding/exit rule the claimant never gave.
